- Security evidence (SOC2, logs, retention, KMS integration)
- PoC scope: latency/throughput tests, token-cost profiling, and model behavior checks on our prompt sets
- Region requirement: US West + failover to US East (data residency constraint)
- Deployment preference: prefer hosted for speed but want viability of Dedicated or Private if compliance needs tighten

Elena — really appreciate the clear asks. I attached a draft MAP and our security checklist to this reply (see attachment stubs below). Summary and proposed timeline: 

Proposed MAP milestones (high level):
1) May 20–21: Align scope & sign MAP (action owners + success criteria)
2) May 22–26: PoC execution (streaming latency test, batch throughput, model QA on 3 prompt categories)
3) May 27: Infra decision call — pick Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (decision window you requested)
4) June 1–30: If Dedicated or Private chosen, initiate capacity reservation + network runbooks; Hosted goes to production configuration and SLA review

PoC scope (deliverables):
- Latency report (p50/p95) for streaming paths and sync generate
- Cost-per-1k-tokens projection across candidate models + quantization notes
- Model regression report for your top-50 prompts (quality gates)
- Security questionnaire evidence (SOC2 excerpts, audit log samples, KMS integration pattern)

Quick notes on hosting guidance: 
- Hosted: fastest to get live; we can do a canary in us-west within 48 hours of PoC signoff. Good for early rollout but limited to our multi-tenant constraints for extremely sensitive data.
- Dedicated: predictable throughput and unit economics; lead time for capacity reservation depends on GPU family and region (cc: Karthik for details).
- Private: viable for regulated workloads; requires network onboarding and likely a 4–8 week ops window depending on on-prem vs VPC.

Attached (stubs): HealthNexus_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP milestones + owners), security_checklist.pdf (SOC2 pointers, evidence list)

Next step: confirm owners for each MAP row and whether we should run the PoC in us-west only or cross-region. I'll loop in Karthik and Priyom internally to confirm capacity, pricing, and private deployment runway.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Quick capacity/ops notes: 
- Dedicated: we can offer a Dedicated pool in us-west (NVL-Accelerator family) with a 2-week provisioning lead time if they commit to minimum monthly capacity (we should discuss sizing in the MAP row). Fallback to us-east is possible but will add cross-region replication for KV caches and a short SLA delta.
- For 2–4k concurrent QPS with streaming workloads I recommend NVL-A100 equivalent (mixed precision) or the newer NVL-P7 for better throughput; we should quantify cost difference in the PoC report.
- Private: for a VPC-hosted private control plane, 4–6 weeks is realistic if networking + CorpNet peering is straightforward; on-prem (air-gapped) is a 6–10 week project depending on hardware procurement and rack scheduling.
- Canary plan: if they accept Hosted for initial release, we can do week-of-May-31 canary (us-west) with a plan to flip traffic to Dedicated in June if contract signatures complete.

I'll attach rough lead-time bullets to the MAP doc and a recommended sizing starter config.

Karthik
Head of Dedicated Ops (internal note in reply)

- Gating items that could push beyond June: formal legal review of data processing addendum (DPA), customer procurement hardware lead times if on-prem, and any custom HSM/KMS procurement.
- Suggest we include an explicit MAP row: "Compliance sign-off (Legal + Infra)" with a hard deadline of May 26 to keep the May 27 decision.

Happy to stand up a 30-minute session with HealthNexus infra next week to walk through the network diagram and KMS options.
